There are mainly 2 types of antinflammatory meds. You got NSAIDs and corticosteroids. NSAID are your normal OTC pills, all analogs of aspirin (ibuprofen, etc.) Corticosteroids (steroids for short but not the same as anabolic steroids) are analogs of the hormone cortisol. Meaning they affect the body like cortisol does, in various degrees of potency depending on the steroid and methylprednisolone being on the stronger side of the spectrum. Steroids induce a more powerful anti-inflammatory response over NSAIDs, which is why they make you feel better. Now why don't we use these long term (at least not for musculoskeletal conditions) is because they effectively shut your immune system down, making you susceptible for infections, great for autoimmune diseases. Second reason for not using long term steroids: Cortisol is one of the hormones made at the adrenal glands on top of the kidneys. If you are using steroids, they adrenals will detect this as high cortisol levels, and respond by shutting down its own cortisol production. Shutting this down long enough will result in adrenal atrophy, rendering the gland unable to produce your own hormones, often irreversibly.

There are other anti-inflammatory meds classes but those are more targeted towards autoimmune diseases and cancer.
